title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives Election in Florida's 2nd Congressional District
description: Florida's 2nd Congressional District seat is open in 2026 after Republican incumbent Neal Dunn announced on January 13, 2026, that he would not seek re-election. The district, covering a large swath of the Florida Panhandle, has been a reliably Republican stronghold, but the open seat has drawn competitive primary fields in both parties. The Republican primary is particularly crowded, with candidates including state GOP chair Evan Power, businessman and veteran Keith Gross, Gulf County Superintendent Jim Norton, and former Rick Scott counsel Austin Rogers. On the Democratic side, Yen Bailey (the 2024 nominee), Brice Barnes, Amanda Green, and Nic Zateslo are among those competing for their party's nomination. The general election will take place on November 3, 2026, with primary elections scheduled for August 18, 2026.
polling_note: No publicly available general election polls were found for this race as of the current date. The primary is not until August 18, 2026, so most polling is still internal or candidate-specific.

candidates.name: Keith Gross
candidates.summary: Keith Gross is a businessman, U.S. Army veteran, and former Assistant State Attorney running for the open seat in Florida's 2nd Congressional District. He was a candidate for the U.S. Senate in Florida in 2024 and has positioned himself as a conservative aligned with President Donald Trump. Gross emphasizes America First policies, border security, and reducing inflation as key campaign issues.

forecast.rationale: No public general-election polls exist for this race (based_on_poll_count=0). The forecast relies entirely on the structural and contextual data provided. Florida's 2nd Congressional District covers a large swath of the Florida Panhandle and is described in the race data as a reliably Republican stronghold. Incumbent Neal Dunn (R) won re-election here in 2024, and the district's fundamentals strongly favor the GOP. However, the seat is open (Dunn announced retirement in January 2026), which increases uncertainty, and both parties have competitive multi-candidate primaries scheduled for August 18, 2026, with no nominee yet selected. The Republican primary field includes prominent figures like state party chair Evan Power, while the Democratic field includes well-funded candidates such as Nic Zateslo ($325K raised) and the 2024 nominee Yen Bailey. Given the district's strong Republican lean but the additional uncertainty from an open seat, competitive primaries, and zero polling, a likely Republican rating (80-94% win probability) with medium confidence and a 16-point margin estimate is appropriate.
